instruction: Insert a column chart in the 'Chart' column for each order ID, utilizing the data from January to March.

metadata.explanation: Task requires creating individual column charts for each order ID using Jan-Mar data and embedding them in the Chart column. Verification extracts order ID count from file (expected number of charts), detects charts via openpyxl (sheet charts and drawing objects), verifies chart types (column charts), and checks data range references (Jan, Feb, Mar columns). Metric compares actual chart count against expected count (one per order ID), verifies chart types and data ranges, providing comprehensive validation of task completion.

llm_judge_reasons: Coverage is complete: Evaluator checks all requirements - chart count per order ID (line 60-66), chart type verification (line 70-78), data range verification (line 81-86), and structure validation (line 45-54)
Expected value calculation is correct: Getter dynamically counts order IDs from file data (line 89: order_id_count = max_row - 1), providing accurate expected chart count
Chart type verification implemented: Lines 125-130 check for ColumnChart instances, correctly verifying the instruction requirement for 'column charts'
Data range verification implemented: Lines 133-144 verify charts reference columns B, C, D (Jan, Feb, Mar), checking correct data source
Weighted scoring is reasonable: Chart count match (40%), structure (35%), chart type (15%), data range (10%) - appropriately weights the critical requirements
Fallback verification provides safety: Lines 93-96 give partial credit (50%) if chart cells have content but charts aren't detected via openpyxl, handling potential detection limitations
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Chart detection method limitation: ws._charts (line 120) detects sheet-level charts, but instruction says 'insert them in the Chart column' which may indicate cell-embedded/anchored charts. Consider testing if openpyxl's ws._charts can detect anchored charts, or investigate ws._drawings more thoroughly (lines 147-154)

Fallback logic could be more robust: Lines 166-180 check for cell content (values, hyperlinks, colors) but embedded charts may not always change these properties. Consider checking for cell.data_type or other chart-specific indicators

Data range assumption: Lines 139-141 assume Order ID is in column A (checks for B, C, D references), but this is validated at line 105 so risk is low. Still, could make this more dynamic by using actual column indices from headers

Unused expected_state parameter: Metric signature (line 4) declares expected_state: List[str] but never uses it (validation is fully dynamic via result_state). This is semantically odd but not incorrect - consider documenting why it's unused or removing it
